source_note: Treatments authored during the hub build (Phase 4) at CAF-student level. verification_status is extracted_unverified throughout: study aids, not verified against official standard text. Worked-example numbers are illustrative.

audit_risk_links.note: Premature recognition is the audit risk that mirrors getting IFRS 15 timing wrong.
Fictitious sales bypass the 'contract + control transferred' discipline.

common_mistakes: Recognising revenue when the order is received or goods are produced, instead of when control transfers.
Recording the full cash collected as revenue when part of it is refundable or belongs to another party (principal vs agent).
Ignoring variable consideration (discounts, rebates, returns) or recognising it without applying the constraint.
Treating a financing component as revenue instead of interest income when payment is deferred significantly.
treatments.disclosure: Disaggregate revenue by category; disclose contract balances (receivables, contract assets/liabilities), performance obligations (when typically satisfied, transaction price allocated to unsatisfied obligations), and significant judgements.
treatments.initial_measurement: Transaction price: the amount the entity expects to be entitled to, net of trade discounts. Variable consideration (discounts, rebates, refunds) is estimated and included only to the extent it is highly probable that a significant reversal will not occur.

journals.narration: Sale on credit at transaction price

treatments.presentation: Revenue presented as a separate line item. Contract assets and contract liabilities presented separately from trade receivables/payables.
treatments.recognition: Revenue is recognised when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation by transferring control of the promised goods to the customer — typically on delivery for a simple sale of goods.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IFRS 15 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Increases revenue and profit in the period of transfer; recognises receivables (unconditional right) or contract assets/liabilities for timing differences on the SFP.
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Contract asset becomes a receivable when the right to consideration is unconditional. Contract liability is derecognised as revenue when the obligation is satisfied.
treatments.title: Revenue from sale of goods
treatments.transaction_analysis: A contract with a customer to transfer goods. Work through five steps: (1) identify the contract, (2) identify each distinct performance obligation, (3) determine the transaction price, (4) allocate the price to the obligations, (5) recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

audit_risk_links.note: Theft, damage and obsolescence are exactly what create NRV write-downs.

common_mistakes: Including abnormal waste, idle storage costs or selling costs in inventory cost.
Carrying obsolete or slow-moving inventory at full cost instead of writing down to NRV.
Valuing inventory at selling price rather than the lower of cost and NRV.
Forgetting that a write-down can be reversed (up to the original cost) if NRV recovers.
treatments.disclosure: Disclose the accounting policy, carrying amounts by category, the amount of any write-down recognised or reversed, and inventories pledged as security.
treatments.initial_measurement: Cost comprises purchase price (net of trade discounts), conversion costs (direct labour + systematic allocation of fixed and variable production overheads based on normal capacity), and other costs incurred in bringing inventories to their present location and condition.

journals.narration: Reversal when NRV recovers (max: original cost)

treatments.presentation: Inventories presented as a current asset, split by category (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods) where material.
treatments.recognition: Inventory is recognised when the entity obtains control — normally on purchase or on completion of production.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IAS 2 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Write-downs reduce profit in the period recognised and reduce current assets; reversals increase profit in a later period.
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV = estimated selling price less estimated costs of completion and estimated costs necessary to make the sale).
treatments.title: Inventories — cost vs net realisable value
treatments.transaction_analysis: Goods held for sale, in production, or as materials. Determine cost, then compare with NRV item-by-item (or by groups of similar items); recognise any write-down immediately.

audit_risk_links.note: Repairs vs capitalisation is the classic IAS 16 audit risk.
Depreciation method, useful life and residual value drive this risk.

common_mistakes: Expensing items that meet the capitalisation criteria (or capitalising day-to-day servicing).
Depreciating land (land is not depreciated; buildings on it are).
Never reviewing useful lives and residual values — they must be reviewed at least annually.
Depreciating a single asset when significant components have different useful lives (component approach required).
treatments.disclosure: Disclose measurement bases, depreciation methods and useful lives/rates, gross carrying amounts and accumulated depreciation, and any restrictions or pledged assets.
treatments.initial_measurement: Cost: purchase price (net of discounts) plus directly attributable costs of bringing the asset to the location and condition for intended use (site preparation, delivery, installation, professional fees) plus the initial estimate of dismantling/restoration costs.
treatments.presentation: PPE presented as non-current assets, analysed by class (land and buildings, plant and equipment, etc.).
treatments.recognition: Recognised when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the cost can be measured reliably. Day-to-day servicing is expensed.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IAS 16 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Capitalisation defers expense recognition (depreciation over useful life) and increases non-current assets; depreciation reduces profit each period.
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Cost model: carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses. Depreciate each significant part separately over its useful life using a method reflecting the pattern of benefits (often straight-line).
treatments.title: PPE — recognition and depreciation (cost model)
treatments.transaction_analysis: Tangible items held for use in production, rental or administration over more than one period. Separate capital expenditure from repairs; identify significant components.

audit_risk_links.note: ROU assets are depreciated like PPE — same estimation risk.

common_mistakes: Keeping operating leases off-balance-sheet out of habit (pre-IFRS 16 thinking).
Using the wrong discount rate (must be the rate implicit in the lease if determinable, otherwise the incremental borrowing rate).
Ignoring extension/termination options that are reasonably certain to be exercised when measuring the liability.
Applying the recognition exemptions to leases that do not qualify (term over 12 months or not low-value).
treatments.disclosure: Disclose the nature of leasing activities, maturity analysis of lease liabilities, and amounts recognised (depreciation, interest, cash outflows).
treatments.initial_measurement: Lease liability: present value of the lease payments not yet paid, discounted as above. ROU asset: liability amount plus initial direct costs, prepayments, less lease incentives received.

journals.narration: Unwinding of discount on the liability

treatments.presentation: ROU assets and lease liabilities presented separately (or within PPE/borrowings with disclosure); interest and depreciation shown separately from the cash payment.
treatments.recognition: At the commencement date the lessee recognises a right-of-use (ROU) asset and a lease liability. Exemptions (expense as incurred instead): short-term leases (12 months or less, no purchase option) and leases of low-value assets.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IFRS 16 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Increases both assets and liabilities at commencement; replaces a single operating-lease expense with depreciation + interest (front-loaded expense profile).
treatments.subsequent_measurement: ROU asset depreciated over the shorter of its useful life and the lease term (unless ownership transfers). Lease liability measured at amortised cost using the effective interest method; remeasured if payments change.
treatments.title: Lessee accounting for leases
treatments.transaction_analysis: A contract conveying the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time. Identify the lease term (including reasonably certain options) and the lease payments.

audit_risk_links.note: Unsupported provision assumptions are this exact audit risk.

common_mistakes: Providing for future operating losses (no present obligation exists).
Recognising a provision for a possible obligation (only disclose as a contingent liability).
Recognising contingent assets before the inflow is virtually certain.
Not discounting long-term provisions where the time value of money is material.
treatments.disclosure: For each class of provision: carrying amounts, movements, uncertainties (major assumptions, expected timing). Contingent liabilities: nature and estimated financial effect unless remote.
treatments.initial_measurement: Best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the reporting date — the amount the entity would rationally pay to settle or transfer it. Discount to present value where the time value of money is material.
treatments.presentation: Provisions presented as liabilities (split current/non-current by expected timing).
treatments.recognition: All three conditions required: (1) a present obligation (legal or constructive) as a result of a past event, (2) a probable outflow of resources, (3) a reliable estimate. Otherwise: disclose as a contingent liability (possible obligation, or present obligation failing (2)/(3)) — do not recognise.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IAS 37 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Recognition reduces profit immediately and increases liabilities; utilisation has no P&L effect; reversals increase profit.
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Review at each reporting date and adjust to the current best estimate; unwind the discount as an interest (finance) cost.
treatments.title: Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets
treatments.transaction_analysis: An uncertain liability or obligation (lawsuit, warranty, onerous contract, decommissioning). Test the three recognition criteria; if any fails, consider contingent-liability disclosure instead.

common_mistakes: Classifying by legal form alone instead of applying the business-model and SPPI tests.
Assuming all debt instruments go to amortised cost (fails when the business model is 'hold to collect and sell' or cash flows are not SPPI).
Forgetting the expected credit loss allowance on amortised-cost and FVOCI debt instruments.
Measuring equity investments at cost without considering fair value (FVPL default; irrevocable FVOCI election available).
treatments.disclosure: Disclose classification basis, fair value hierarchy levels, credit risk and ECL allowance, and gains/losses by category.
treatments.initial_measurement: Initially at fair value plus transaction costs (except FVPL, where transaction costs go to profit or loss).

journals.narration: Purchase of debt instrument (hold to collect, SPPI)
Interest recognised by the effective interest method

treatments.presentation: Financial assets split between current and non-current by maturity/expectation; ECL allowance shown against the asset (or in OCI for FVOCI debt).
treatments.recognition: Recognised when the entity becomes a party to the contractual provisions of the instrument (trade date or settlement date accounting).
treatments.source_note: High-level study aid; verify against the official IFRS 9 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Classification decides where value changes hit: profit or loss (FVPL, amortised-cost interest/ECL) vs other comprehensive income (FVOCI).
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Amortised cost: effective interest method less expected credit losses. FVOCI: fair value with changes in OCI (recycled for debt, not for equity). FVPL: fair value with changes in profit or loss.
treatments.title: Financial assets — classification and measurement (essentials)
treatments.transaction_analysis: A contractual right to receive cash or another financial asset. Apply two tests: (1) business model — hold to collect, hold to collect and sell, or other; (2) SPPI — are the contractual cash flows solely payments of principal and interest?

audit_risk_links.note: Unrecognised impairment losses are this exact audit risk.

common_mistakes: Testing goodwill only when indicators exist (goodwill must be tested annually).
Comparing carrying amount with only one of FVLCD / value in use instead of the higher of the two.
Using inconsistent assumptions between cash-flow projections and the discount rate (e.g., pre-tax cash flows with a post-tax rate).
Skipping the CGU level when an asset does not generate independent cash inflows.
treatments.disclosure: Disclose the events causing impairment, the amount of the loss, the recoverable-amount basis used, and key assumptions (discount rates, growth rates) for material impairments.
treatments.initial_measurement: Not an initial-measurement topic: impairment is a subsequent-measurement test. Recoverable amount = the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use (present value of future cash flows from continuing use and disposal).
treatments.presentation: Impairment losses presented within profit or loss (or as a revaluation decrease if the asset is carried under the revaluation model).
treatments.recognition: Recognise an impairment loss when the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount. Test goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles annually even without indicators.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IAS 36 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Reduces profit in the period and reduces the asset's carrying amount (future depreciation is based on the reduced amount).
treatments.subsequent_measurement: After impairment, depreciate the revised carrying amount over the remaining useful life. Reversals are permitted for most assets (never for goodwill) up to the carrying amount that would have existed without the impairment.
treatments.title: Impairment of non-financial assets
treatments.transaction_analysis: At each reporting date, assess whether indicators of impairment exist (market declines, adverse technological/market changes, obsolescence, worse-than-expected performance). If indicators exist — or annually for goodwill — compare carrying amount with recoverable amount.

common_mistakes: Discounting deferred tax balances (prohibited).
Recognising a deferred tax asset without convincing evidence of future taxable profits.
Offsetting deferred tax assets and liabilities without a legally enforceable right and same-tax-authority conditions.
Forgetting deferred tax on revaluations and business combinations.
treatments.disclosure: Disclose the tax expense split (current/deferred), a reconciliation of accounting profit to tax expense, and unrecognised deferred tax assets.
treatments.initial_measurement: Current tax: the tax payable on this period's taxable profit per enacted tax law. Deferred tax: temporary difference × the tax rate expected to apply when the asset is realised or liability settled.

journals.narration: Deferred tax on taxable temporary differences
Deferred tax on deductible temporary differences (probable recovery)

treatments.presentation: Current and deferred tax balances presented separately; deferred tax is always non-current and never discounted; offset only when strict conditions are met.
treatments.recognition: Current tax recognised as a liability (or asset if paid in advance). Deferred tax liability for all taxable temporary differences; deferred tax asset for deductible temporary differences, unused losses and credits — only to the extent probable future taxable profit is available.
treatments.source_note: Study aid; verify against the official IAS 12 text.
treatments.statement_impact: Tax expense reduces profit; deferred tax balances adjust the SFP without affecting current-period cash tax.
treatments.subsequent_measurement: Remeasure deferred tax when tax rates change (effect goes to the same place the original did — usually profit or loss). Review deferred tax assets each period for recoverability.
treatments.title: Income taxes — current and deferred tax
treatments.transaction_analysis: Differences between accounting profit and taxable profit. Identify temporary differences (carrying amount vs tax base): taxable ones create deferred tax liabilities, deductible ones create deferred tax assets (subject to the probability test).
